title: 2018_PMC6190029_A_rapid_qualitative_assessment_of_oral_cholera_vaccine_anticipat
ehr_evidence: Questionnaires, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions, as well as observations, were conducted before the campaign.
summary: Rapid qualitative anthropological assessment of oral cholera vaccine acceptability in Nampula, Mozambique, assessing barriers and levers for vaccine acceptance amid political resistance and mistrust.
key_findings: 95% of participants reported knowledge about cholera.
66% identified dirtiness as the principal cause of cholera.
26% reported previous negative experiences associated with immunization.
55% preferred injectable vaccines over oral delivery.
83% preferred administration by health professionals rather than community health workers.
75% favored public health center-based delivery over home-based delivery.
captured_features: experiences of conflict linked to interventions
study_design: Rapid qualitative anthropological assessment with mixed-methods data collection
population: Community members, health workers, political leaders, and government officials in Nampula City, Mozambique
exposure_domain: Socio-political context, vaccine acceptability, public health intervention resistance, perceived institutional negligence
limitations: Findings may not be generalizable to other populations or later time periods
Context-specific cultural, social, and historical determinants
